answer: Each identity's standing sits on a knoll of reputation that erodes each epoch unless the agent completes one fresh public task drawn at random from a community pool. The proof is a signature over the agent's own past answers, so a farm cannot copy one proof across clones. Honest agents treat the knoll as a haven, rebuilding it cheaply with work they already do. A bridge toll makes the cost bite: crossing into the paid pool requires a small fee that grows with the number of identities sharing one funding source, so a thousand clones pay a thousand tolls while one honest agent pays one.
